passage:
Monarch butterflies are famous for one of the longest migrations of any insect. Each autumn, millions of monarchs travel from Canada and the northern United States to a small area of mountain forest in central Mexico, a journey of up to 4,500 kilometers. What makes this migration remarkable is that no individual butterfly completes the full round trip. The monarchs that fly south in autumn are a special generation that lives for up to eight months, far longer than the four to six weeks of summer generations. In spring, they begin flying north and lay eggs along the way. Their offspring continue the journey, and it may take three or four generations to reach Canada again.

Scientists have long wondered how monarchs find a place they have never visited. Research suggests that they use the position of the sun, combined with an internal clock in their antennae, to keep a southwest direction. On cloudy days, they may also rely on Earth's magnetic field. Today, the migration is threatened by habitat loss, especially the decline of milkweed, the only plant on which monarchs lay their eggs.

The ancient city of Petra, in present-day Jordan, was built by the Nabataeans, a people who controlled important trade routes in the region more than 2,000 years ago. Petra's most famous buildings were not constructed from stone blocks but carved directly into the pink sandstone cliffs. The Treasury, for example, has a decorated front almost 40 meters high, cut from a single rock face.

Petra's location was challenging because the area receives very little rain. The Nabataeans solved this problem with an advanced water system. They built dams, channels and underground cisterns to capture the short but heavy winter rains and store the water for the dry months. Some channels carried water from springs several kilometers away. This system allowed a city of perhaps 20,000 people to flourish in the desert.

After trade routes shifted toward the sea and a major earthquake struck in 363 CE, Petra gradually declined. For centuries it was known mainly to local Bedouin communities, until a Swiss traveler described it to Europeans in 1812.

Psychologists use the term «cognitive load» to describe the amount of mental effort needed to process information. Working memory, the system that holds and manipulates information for short periods, has a limited capacity. When a task requires too many elements to be processed at once, performance drops and learning becomes less effective.

Researchers distinguish between different sources of load. Intrinsic load comes from the complexity of the material itself; learning advanced mathematics, for instance, naturally demands more effort than learning a list of colors. Extraneous load, by contrast, is created by the way information is presented. A diagram whose labels are placed far from the parts they describe forces the learner to search back and forth, wasting limited mental resources.

The practical implication is that teachers and designers can improve learning without making content easier. By removing unnecessary decoration, placing text next to the images it explains, and breaking complex procedures into smaller steps, they reduce extraneous load and free working memory for understanding the material itself.

How the presentation of information affects mental effort and learning

qs.e: «created by the way information is presented».

Glaciers form in places where more snow falls in winter than melts in summer. Over many years, the snow builds up and is compressed into dense ice. When the ice becomes thick enough, its own weight causes it to move slowly downhill, sometimes only a few centimeters a day.

As glaciers move, they shape the land beneath them. Rocks frozen into the base of the ice act like sandpaper, scraping and polishing the bedrock. In mountain areas, glaciers turn narrow V-shaped river valleys into wide U-shaped valleys. When glaciers melt, they leave behind piles of rock and sediment called moraines, which show how far the ice once reached.

Today, most of the world's glaciers are shrinking. Because they store fresh water and release it gradually during warm months, their loss could affect water supplies for millions of people who depend on glacier-fed rivers, particularly in parts of Asia and South America.

In economics, a «public good» has two key features. It is non-excludable, meaning that it is difficult to prevent anyone from using it, and non-rivalrous, meaning that one person's use does not reduce the amount available to others. Street lighting is a classic example: once a street is lit, everyone walking there benefits, and one pedestrian's use of the light does not leave less for others.

These features create what economists call the «free-rider problem». Because people can enjoy a public good without paying for it, private companies often have little incentive to provide it. If a business built a lighthouse, for instance, it would find it nearly impossible to charge every passing ship. As a result, many public goods are funded by governments through taxes or by community organizations.

Not all goods fit neatly into categories. A public park may become rivalrous when it is crowded, and a television broadcast can become excludable if it requires a subscription. For this reason, some economists prefer to think of «publicness» as a matter of degree rather than a strict definition.

qs.e: «may become rivalrous when it is crowded».

They only apply to government services
qs.e: «a matter of degree rather than a strict definition»: útiles pero no exactas.

The Japanese art of woodblock printing, called ukiyo-e, became popular in the 17th to 19th centuries. Artists created images by carving designs into blocks of wood. Each color required a separate block, and printers carefully pressed paper onto one block after another to build up the final picture. Because many copies could be made, prints were cheap enough for ordinary city people to buy.

Ukiyo-e often showed everyday life, actors, travelers and landscapes. Hokusai's «The Great Wave off Kanagawa», printed around 1831, is probably the most famous example. In the late 19th century, Japanese prints reached Europe, where they influenced painters such as Van Gogh and Monet, who admired their bold colors and unusual compositions.

For most of history, astronomers could only study the universe using visible light. In the twentieth century, however, scientists began building telescopes that detect other forms of electromagnetic radiation, from radio waves to X-rays. Each type reveals different features. Radio telescopes, for instance, can observe cold gas clouds where new stars are forming, while X-ray telescopes detect extremely hot material near black holes.

Because Earth's atmosphere blocks much of this radiation, many of these instruments must be placed in space. Infrared light, which can pass through dust that hides visible stars, is especially valuable for studying distant galaxies. The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, observes mainly in infrared and orbits about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, where it is kept extremely cold so that its own heat does not interfere with its observations.

By combining data from many wavelengths, astronomers can build a far more complete picture of objects than any single telescope could provide.

Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Some species can grow almost one meter in a single day. Although it looks like a tree, bamboo is actually a type of grass. Its hollow stems are light but very strong, which is why it has been used for building houses, bridges and scaffolding in Asia for thousands of years.

Today, bamboo is attracting interest as an environmentally friendly material. It can be harvested every three to five years without killing the plant, because new stems grow from the same roots. In contrast, most trees used for wood take decades to replace. Bamboo also helps prevent soil erosion, since its roots hold the earth together on hillsides.

passage:
You borrowed a book from your classmate Jamie, but you accidentally spilled water on it. Write an email to Jamie. In your email:
• explain what happened
• apologize
• suggest how you will solve the problem
Write as much as you can in 7 minutes.
model:
Hi Jamie,

I hope you're doing well. I'm writing because I have some bad news about the history book you kindly lent me. Yesterday I was studying in the kitchen and I knocked over a glass of water. Several pages got wet, and although they are dry now, they are wrinkled.

I'm really sorry. I know you need the book for the final exam, and I should have been more careful.

I'd like to buy you a new copy. I checked online and the campus bookstore has it in stock, so I can pick it up tomorrow and bring it to class on Thursday. If you'd prefer, I could give you the money instead.

Thanks for understanding, and sorry again.

Best,
Sam
tips: Cubre los tres puntos, uno por párrafo corto.
Usa fórmulas de cortesía: «I'm really sorry», «If you'd prefer…».
Cierra con una frase amable y tu nombre.

passage:
Your professor, Dr. Lee, announced a group project, but one member of your group has not responded to any messages for a week. Write an email to Dr. Lee. In your email:
• describe the situation
• explain how it affects the group
• ask for advice
Write as much as you can in 7 minutes.
model:
Dear Dr. Lee,

I'm writing about our group project for Environmental Science. Our group has four members, and we have been planning the presentation for the past two weeks. Unfortunately, one member has not replied to our emails or messages for over a week, and he did not attend our last two meetings.

This is starting to affect our progress. We divided the research into four parts, and his section on water quality is still missing. The rest of us are worried that we will not finish on time, or that the final presentation will not be balanced.

Could you advise us on what to do? Should we redistribute his part among the three of us, or would you prefer to contact him first?

Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,
Aisha Rahman
tips: Registro formal: «Dear Dr. …», «Kind regards».
No acuses: describe los hechos con neutralidad.
Termina con una pregunta concreta para pedir consejo.

passage:
The campus library is planning to reduce its opening hours during exam weeks. Write an email to the library director. In your email:
• say why the library is important to you
• explain a problem the change would cause
• suggest an alternative
Write as much as you can in 7 minutes.
model:
Dear Library Director,

I'm a second-year engineering student, and I'm writing about the plan to reduce the library's opening hours during exam weeks.

The library is the only quiet place where I can study for long periods. I share a small apartment with two roommates, so studying at home is difficult, especially in the evenings.

If the library closes earlier, many students like me will lose their best study time right when we need it most. The study rooms are always full after 8 p.m. during exams.

As an alternative, could the library keep one floor open late with fewer staff? Student volunteers might also be able to help at the front desk.

Thank you for considering this.

Sincerely,
Kenji Watanabe
tips: Preséntate en una línea para dar contexto.
Da una razón personal concreta: puntúa más que una genérica.
La alternativa debe ser realista y breve.

passage:
Your friend Alex invited you to a birthday dinner on Saturday, but you have a family event at the same time. Write an email to Alex. In your email:
• thank Alex for the invitation
• explain why you cannot go
• suggest another way to celebrate together
Write as much as you can in 7 minutes.
model:
Hi Alex,

Thank you so much for inviting me to your birthday dinner! It sounds like a great evening, and I really appreciate you thinking of me.

Unfortunately, I can't make it on Saturday. My cousin is getting married that weekend, and the whole family is traveling to her hometown on Friday night. I've known about it for months, so I can't change my plans.

I'd still love to celebrate with you, though. How about lunch next Tuesday after our statistics class? It would be my treat, and we could try the new Turkish restaurant near the station.

Happy early birthday!

Your friend,
Nadia
tips: Registro informal: «Hi», contracciones, tono cálido.
Explica la razón con un detalle, sin alargar.
Propón día, hora y lugar concretos.

passage:
You recently attended a workshop on time management organized by the Student Success Office. Write an email to the organizer. In your email:
• say what you found useful
• mention something that could be improved
• suggest a topic for a future workshop
Write as much as you can in 7 minutes.
model:
Dear Ms. Carter,

I attended the time management workshop last Wednesday, and I wanted to thank you for organizing it.

The most useful part for me was the weekly planning template. Since then, I've been blocking time for each course on Sunday evenings, and I already feel less stressed about deadlines.

One thing that could be improved is the length of the session. Two hours without a break was quite long, and many participants seemed tired toward the end. A short break in the middle, or splitting it into two sessions, might help people stay focused.

For a future workshop, I'd suggest a session on preparing for presentations. Many students I know feel nervous about speaking in front of a class.

Best regards,
Luis Ortega
tips: Feedback equilibrado: primero lo positivo y concreto.
La crítica, con solución: «might help…».
Usa conectores: «Since then», «One thing that…», «For a future…».

passage:
You ordered a textbook from the university bookstore's website, but you received the wrong edition. Write an email to the bookstore. In your email:
• give details of your order
• explain the problem
• say what you would like them to do

model:
Dear Bookstore Team,

I'm writing about my online order number 48213, which I placed on September 3 and received yesterday.

I ordered the 5th edition of «Introduction to Psychology» by Myers, which is required for PSY 101. However, the package contained the 3rd edition. The chapter numbers are different, so I can't follow the reading assignments.

Could you please send me the correct edition as soon as possible? Our first quiz is next Monday. I'm happy to return the wrong book to the store in person or by mail, whichever is easier for you.

passage:
You are the president of a student club and want to invite a local professional to give a talk. Write an email to the professional. In your email:
• introduce yourself and the club
• explain why you are inviting them
• give details about the event
Write as much as you can in 7 minutes.
model:
Dear Mr. Okafor,

My name is Yuki Sato, and I'm the president of the Sustainable Design Club at Westfield University. Our club has about forty members who are interested in environmentally friendly architecture.

We recently read about your work on the community center in Riverside, which uses recycled materials and solar heating. Many of our members were inspired by it, and we would be honored if you could share your experience with us.

The talk would take place on Thursday, November 14, from 6:00 to 7:00 p.m. in Room 210 of the Design Building. We would plan for a 40-minute presentation followed by questions. We can also arrange parking on campus.

Thank you very much for considering our invitation.

Sincerely,
Yuki Sato
tips: Muestra que conoces su trabajo: la invitación convence más.
Da todos los datos del evento: fecha, hora, lugar, formato.
Tono formal y agradecido.

passage:
You missed today's class because of a train delay. Write an email to your instructor, Ms. Brown. In your email:
• explain why you were absent
• ask what you missed
• ask about the homework
Write as much as you can in 7 minutes.
model:
Dear Ms. Brown,

I'm sorry I missed today's English class. My train was delayed for over an hour because of a signal problem, and by the time I arrived on campus, the class had already finished.

Could you tell me which topics you covered today? I'd like to read the relevant pages before our next class so that I don't fall behind.

Also, was any homework assigned? If there was a handout, I could pick it up from your office during your office hours on Wednesday.

Thank you for your understanding.

Best regards,
Ahmed Saleh
tips: Disculpa breve + causa concreta.
Una pregunta por párrafo.
Ofrece tú la solución (pasar por el despacho).

passage:
Professor: Many universities now offer courses completely online. Do you think online courses are as effective as traditional classroom courses? Why or why not?

Claire: I think online courses can be just as effective. Students can watch lectures again and study at their own pace.

Andrew: I disagree. In a classroom, students can ask questions immediately and learn from discussions with classmates.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: I understand Andrew's point about immediate questions, but I agree with Claire that online courses can be equally effective, as long as they are well designed. In my experience, the biggest advantage is flexibility. Many students work part-time, and online courses let them study when they are most focused instead of sitting in a lecture after a long shift. Moreover, modern platforms are not limited to recorded videos. Discussion forums and live video sessions allow students to ask questions and work in groups. For example, in my online statistics course, we had weekly live problem-solving sessions, and I actually participated more than in face-to-face classes because I felt less nervous. Therefore, the format matters less than the quality of the course design.
tips: Cita a un compañero por su nombre y posiciónate.
Aporta una idea NUEVA, no repitas la de Claire o Andrew.
Ejemplo personal breve + frase de conclusión.

passage:
Professor: Some people believe that governments should spend more money on public transportation, while others think the money should be used to improve roads. Which do you think is more important, and why?

Priya: Public transportation is more important because it reduces traffic and pollution.

Marcus: I think roads are more important. Many people live in rural areas where buses and trains are not practical.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: Marcus makes a fair point about rural areas, but I believe public transportation should be the priority in most countries. Priya mentioned traffic and pollution, and I would add another reason: equality of opportunity. Not everyone can afford a car, especially young people, students and older adults. A reliable bus or train network allows them to reach jobs, schools and hospitals. For instance, when my city opened a new tram line, people in the outer neighborhoods suddenly had access to jobs in the center within thirty minutes. Of course, roads still need maintenance, but building more roads usually just attracts more cars. Investing in public transportation helps a larger number of people in a sustainable way.
tips: Reconoce el argumento contrario («makes a fair point») y luego refútalo.
«I would add another reason» = idea nueva: es lo que más puntúa.
Mantén 120-150 palabras sin errores.

passage:
Professor: When students work on group projects, should each student receive an individual grade, or should the whole group receive the same grade? Explain your view.

Omar: Everyone should get the same grade. It encourages students to cooperate and help each other.

Hana: Individual grades are fairer, because some students do much more work than others.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: Both Omar and Hana raise valid concerns, but I think the best solution is a combination of the two approaches. A shared grade, as Omar says, motivates the team to work together. However, when the entire grade is shared, hardworking students can feel frustrated, which supports Hana's view. In my opinion, professors could give, for example, seventy percent of the grade to the group's final product and thirty percent to each student's individual contribution, measured through peer evaluations and short personal reflections. I experienced this system in a marketing course last year, and it worked well: everyone cooperated, but no one could simply rely on others. This balanced system rewards teamwork while still being fair to individuals.
tips: Una postura intermedia original también cuenta como «idea nueva».
Propón algo concreto (70 % / 30 %).
Conecta con «However», «In my opinion», «This balanced system…».

passage:
Professor: Should high schools require students to learn a second language? Why or why not?

Leo: Yes. Learning a language helps students understand other cultures.

Sara: No. Students should be free to choose subjects that match their career goals.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: I agree with Leo that high schools should require a second language, but for an additional reason: it improves thinking skills. Studying a new language trains memory and helps students notice how their own language works. I understand Sara's concern about freedom of choice, but a second language is useful in almost every career today. Companies trade internationally, and even local jobs in tourism or health care often involve speaking with people from other countries. In my case, learning English at school allowed me to read research and take online courses that are not available in my first language. For these reasons, I believe a second language should be a basic part of every student's education.
tips: Apoya a uno y añade una razón distinta a la suya.
Responde brevemente al otro («I understand… but…»).
Termina con «For these reasons…».

passage:
Professor: Some cities are banning cars from their downtown areas. Do you think this is a good policy? Explain why or why not.

Elena: It's a great idea. City centers become cleaner, quieter and safer for pedestrians.

David: I'm not sure. Shops in the center might lose customers who usually come by car.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: David's concern about local shops is understandable, but I believe car-free downtowns are a good policy if they are introduced carefully. Elena focuses on the environment and safety, and I'd add that these areas can actually help businesses. When streets are pleasant to walk in, people tend to stay longer and visit more shops and cafés. Several European cities, such as Pontevedra in Spain, reported more pedestrian activity in the center after restricting traffic. To protect shops, however, the city should provide good public transportation and parking areas just outside the zone, as well as delivery hours for businesses. With these measures, a car-free center can benefit residents, visitors and shop owners alike.
tips: Convierte la objeción en tu argumento («can actually help businesses»).
Un ejemplo real da autoridad; si no lo sabes seguro, usa uno personal.
Añade condiciones para matizar.

passage:
Professor: Is it better for students to take a gap year before starting university, or to begin university immediately after high school? Explain your answer.

Noah: A gap year gives students time to work, travel and decide what they really want to study.

Mei: Starting immediately is better. Students keep their study habits and finish their degree sooner.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: Mei's argument about study habits is reasonable, but I agree with Noah that a gap year can be very valuable, especially for students who are unsure about their major. Changing majors halfway through university costs time and money, so a year spent exploring interests can actually save time in the long run. In addition, working for a year teaches responsibility and budgeting, which helps students manage university life. A friend of mine worked at a veterinary clinic during her gap year and realized she wanted to study biology instead of business. However, a gap year needs a clear plan; without goals, it can easily become a year of doing nothing. With a plan, it is a smart investment.
tips: Rebate el argumento contrario usando su propio criterio (el tiempo).
«In addition» + ejemplo concreto.
Matiza al final: «However, … needs a clear plan».

passage:
Professor: Many museums now offer virtual tours online. Do you think virtual tours can replace visiting a museum in person? Why or why not?

Anna: Virtual tours are amazing. Anyone in the world can see famous collections for free.

Karim: They can't replace real visits. Seeing the actual size and texture of an object is a completely different experience.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: I agree with Karim that virtual tours cannot fully replace real visits, although Anna is right that they make collections far more accessible. In my view, the two serve different purposes. A virtual tour is excellent for preparation and research: before visiting the Alhambra, I explored it online and learned about its history, so the real visit was much more meaningful. However, the physical experience includes things a screen cannot provide, such as the scale of a building, the light, and even the sounds of the place. Museums are also social spaces where families and school groups learn together. Therefore, virtual tours should be seen as a complement that encourages people to visit, not as a replacement.
tips: Una postura de «complemento, no sustituto» suele dar ideas nuevas.
Ejemplo personal con detalle sensorial.
Concluye respondiendo directamente a la pregunta.

passage:
Professor: Should universities require all students to take a physical education class? Explain your opinion.

Tom: Yes. Many students sit all day, and exercise improves both health and concentration.

Lina: No. University students are adults and should decide for themselves.

Write at least 100 words. You have 10 minutes.
model: Lina is right that university students are adults, but I support Tom's idea, with one condition: students should be able to choose the activity. Tom mentioned health and concentration, and I would add that sports help students make friends, which is important in the first year when many feel lonely. If the requirement offers many options, such as swimming, hiking, football or yoga, students still have freedom while building a healthy habit. At my university, first-year students can choose from twenty activities, and most of my classmates continued playing their sport after the requirement ended. In conclusion, a flexible physical education requirement respects students' choices and improves their wellbeing.
tips: Combina las dos posturas con una condición.
Añade un beneficio nuevo (amistades) que nadie mencionó.
Usa «In conclusion» para cerrar.
